articles.summary: Fermi Inc. has issued $431.25 million in aggregate principal amount of 5.00% convertible senior notes due 2031, with total net proceeds of approximately $416.81 million, which will be used for general corporate purposes. The notes are convertible into cash, shares of common stock, or a combination thereof, at the company's election, with an initial conversion price of approximately $9.52 per share. The company also entered into capped call transactions to reduce potential dilution to its common stock upon conversion of the notes, using approximately $34.5 million of the net proceeds to pay for these transactions.

articles.title: SEC filing: 8-K — Fermi Inc. (CURRENT REPORT)
articles.summary: Fermi Inc. discloses the immediate resignation of director Miles Everson, effective July 10, 2026, due to a disagreement over access to company books and records and the delegation of financing transaction oversight to the Finance Committee. Everson's resignation was submitted in a letter, which is attached to the filing as an exhibit, and he did not serve on any committee of the Board at the time of his resignation. The company believes Everson was granted full access to its books and records, except for certain litigation-related materials, and had previously approved the establishment of the Finance Committee.

articles.title: SEC filing: 8-K — Fermi Inc. (CURRENT REPORT)
articles.summary: Fermi Inc. commenced an offering of $350 million in convertible senior notes due 2031 to qualified institutional buyers, with an option for the initial purchasers to buy an additional $52.5 million in notes. Fermi Inc. also disclosed that it has deferred its planned election to be taxed as a real estate investment trust, and now expects to make this election for its taxable year ending December 31, 2026, if it qualifies.

articles.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed in response to his challenge of the validity of the company's 70% supermajority bylaw. This move comes after the Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw, and Neugebauer claims that the company's decision to abandon the lawsuit confirms that the bylaw was adopted to entrench the board's power. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

articles.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi America, delivered an investor presentation on June 30, 2026, discussing his concerns about the company's contracts and governance. Neugebauer emphasized the importance of having the right team to steward contracts, which can be either assets or liabilities, and expressed his desire for an independent committee and a banker-led market test to ensure evidence-based decision-making. He also stated that he is not interested in returning to the company, but rather wants to ensure that the board prioritizes the interests of shareholders.
